newsitem.title: USA: U.S. dollar policy unchanged, Rubin says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar policy unchanged, Rubin says.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Tuesday said that U.S. policy on the dollar remains unchanged.

"Our policy has been sound and sensible and well-articulated many times," Rubin told a news conference on an administrative initiative to clean up polluted industrial sites. "There has been no change in our policy."
Vice President Gore, who was also at the news conference, then chimed in, "Terrific answer."

Rubin in the past has frequently propounded the value of a strong dollar for the U.S. economy because it keeps inflation and interest rates down. However, recently he has signalled his desire for a stronger Japanese yen.

The dollar has fallen sharply against the Japanese yen in the past week, in part spurred by the belief that both the United States and Japan wanted to see it lower to avoid a big rise in Japan's trade surplus.

But the speed of the decline has surprised Japanese officials. Earlier on Tuesday, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka signalled his desire for the dollar to stabilize after its recent sharp fall, saying he expected to settle down soon.
Asked if he agreed with Mitsuzuka's comments, Rubin ducked the question and instead said U.S. currency policy was unchanged.
